Computing – Desktop vs Laptop Energy Use
Compare energy usage of computing devices
Computers are an essential part of modern life. They are used for studying, gaming, communication and entertainment. However, different types of computers consume very different amounts of energy.
Understanding these differences helps users make more sustainable choices while balancing performance and energy efficiency.

Desktop computers generally use more electricity because they contain larger processors, dedicated graphics cards and external monitors. Laptops are designed to maximise battery life, making them more energy efficient.
A typical desktop computer may consume between 150 and 300 watts during operation, while a laptop may use between 20 and 60 watts.
Although desktops often offer greater performance, laptops can provide significant energy savings over time.
This represents a substantial reduction in energy use and environmental impact.
